title: A monic Eisenstein quotient of a DVR is a DVR
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring and $\pi$ a uniformizer [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $n\geq1$ and let $P(T)=T^n+\sum_{i<n}a_iT^i\in R[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] satisfy $a_i\in\pi R$ for all $i<n$ and $a_0\in\pi R\setminus\pi^2R$. Put $C=R[T]/(P)$ and write $x$ for the class of $T$. Then $C$ is a discrete valuation ring and $\mathfrak m_C=xC$. No completeness, separability, or residue-characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: last sentence: B[t]/(P(t)) is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer the class of t

proof.text: The DVR is a local PID and therefore Noetherian and a unique factorization domain. Monicity and the coefficient hypotheses make P Eisenstein at the prime maximal ideal (pi). Apply Mathlib Polynomial.IsEisensteinAt.irreducible to the primitive positive-degree polynomial P. In the polynomial UFD P is prime; AdjoinRoot.isDomain_of_prime gives that C=AdjoinRoot P is a domain. The monic power-basis lemma makes C finite over R, hence integral and Noetherian. Positive degree makes the constants map injective.

source.place: Tag 09ER, final sentence of lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified; expanded using Mathlib Eisenstein irreducibility and the residue-quotient argument

proof.text: Write a_0=pi*u. If u is a nonunit then u belongs to (pi), so a_0 belongs to (pi^2), a contradiction; thus u is a unit. Let J=(x) and theta:C->C/J. Apply theta to P(x)=0. Since theta(x)=0, theta(a_0)=0. Cancelling the image of the unit u gives theta(pi)=0. Evaluation at zero modulo pi defines a surjection phi:C->R/(pi). The constants map R->C/J factors through a map psi:R/(pi)->C/J. The composite psi*phi equals theta, since it agrees on constants and x. Consequently ker(phi)=J, so J is maximal.

source.place: Tag 09ER, final sentence of lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified; expanded using Mathlib Eisenstein irreducibility and the residue-quotient argument

proof.text: For a maximal ideal M of C, integrality makes its contraction maximal in R, hence equal to (pi). The polynomial relation and the lower coefficient hypotheses give x^n in (pi)C, using Polynomial.IsWeaklyEisensteinAt.pow_natDegree_le_of_aeval_zero_of_monic_mem_map. Thus x^n belongs to M. Primality gives x in M, whence J is contained in M and the maximality of J forces M=J. Therefore C is local and its maximal ideal is J.

source.place: Tag 09ER, final sentence of lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified; expanded using Mathlib Eisenstein irreducibility and the residue-quotient argument

proof.text: If x=0, evaluating P at the root gives a_0=0 in C. Injectivity of the constants map gives a_0=0 in R, contradicting a_0 not in (pi^2). The Noetherian local domain C thus has maximal ideal generated by the nonzero element x. Apply the principal-maximal-ideal criterion to obtain its DVR structure, together with the already proved maximal-ideal equality.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09ER final assertion, proved in Lean by direct Mathlib Eisenstein irreducibility, finite monic quotient, residue quotient and unique maximal ideal, then Tag 00PD. K2, 2026-10-26. This replaces the original intersection-of-powers domain argument.

lean.statement: theorem adjoinRoot_of_monic_eisenstein (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] (π : R) (hπ : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R = Ideal.span {π}) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (P : Polynomial R) (hP : P.Monic) (hdeg : P.natDegree = n) (hcoeff : ∀ i : ℕ, i < n → P.coeff i ∈ Ideal.span {π}) (hconst : P.coeff 0 ∉ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) : ∃ (_ : IsDomain (AdjoinRoot P)) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing (AdjoinRoot P)), IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (AdjoinRoot P) = Ideal.span {AdjoinRoot.root P}

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches node and Stacks 09ER (l.34500-34514) clause by clause: DVR R via Mathlib IsDiscreteValuationRing, uniformizer as maximalIdeal = span{π}, monic P with natDegree n ≥ 1, a_i ∈ (π) for i<n, a_0 ∉ (π^2); C = AdjoinRoot P, x = root P; conclusion ∃ IsDomain, ∃ IsDVR, maximalIdeal = span{root P}. No extra hypotheses or universe restriction. Edge cases n=1, n=0 excluded, T^2 excluded, inseparable case included.
